The paper presents a 3D visible-light invisibility cloak.
The cloak is designed using a polyhedral transformation method.
The experiment demonstrates the cloaking effect using a cubic shape and a steel ball as the object to be hidden.
The compression ratio of the cloak is 0.172.
The wavelength of the laser beam used in the experiment is 532 nm.
The shape of the object to be hidden is a steel ball.
The cloak can guide light around a hidden object and make it return to its original path when incident from certain 3D perpendicular directions.
The cloak has significant implications for surveillance technology and security-related purposes.
The polyhedral transformation method allows for a homogeneous grid for each segment.
The quasiconformal mapping method results in an inhomogeneous grid.
The cloak is designed to work in three orthogonal directions in 3D space.
The cloak can hide an object from plain sight in visible light from any viewpoint.
The main obstacle to creating an invisibility cloak is the coupling of the electromagnetic components of light.
Transformation optics is a theory that uses a mathematical transformation to design materials with specific properties to manipulate light.
The paper was published in Advanced Science in 2018.
